🇲🇽🌎 <u>UN chief: Mexico, a historic ally of the United Nations</u>

Closing Mexico's week at the 81st UN General Assembly, Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco met António Guterres, who highlighted Mexico's historic role as an ally of the UN and the weight of its support for the future of the multilateral system.

Guterres recognized Mexico's respect for international law and its backing of the UN80 reform, and sent greetings to President Sheinbaum for her work "to bring well-being to the Mexican people." Both defended the peaceful resolution of conflicts and the legal equality of states — the Estrada Doctrine, still written into Mexico's Constitution.
banner: UN CHIEF: MEXICO, A HISTORIC ALLY

text:
🇲🇽🌎 <u>No foreign power decides Mexico's destiny</u>

From Sonora, before more than 20,000 people, Sheinbaum closed the penultimate stop of her "Honesty and Results" tour with a message aimed north: "Only the Mexican people determine their destiny. No foreign power determines Mexico's destiny, no elite determines the destiny of the nation."

On the powers still eyeing Mexico's natural resources: "Here the people are always present, with their history, with their memory, defending the homeland." Said in the state that holds Mexico's nationalized lithium.

🇲🇽🌎 "Only the people of Mexico determine their destiny. No foreign power determines the destiny of Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Hermosillo, Sonora In Hermosillo she went back to Morelos' Sentimientos de la Nación: "moderate indigence and opulence," and "the son of the laborer and the son of the landowner must have the same education." Its principle "sovereignty emanates from the people" is today Article 39 of the Constitution. "No elite determines the destiny of the homeland," she added. "Democracy is not the democracy of a few; it is the people in their government."

🇲🇽✊ "Older adults are heroes and heroines of the homeland." "Those who are against us say we shouldn't be giving money away. That's false. It is not given away. It is returning to the people the money the people paid in taxes." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Morelia, Michoacán In Michoacán, 606,788 older adults receive the universal pension. Answering a former president who called pension recipients lazy, she said Indigenous peoples venerate their elders, and that only in Mexico do all adults 65 and over have a pension, now a constitutional right.

🇲🇽❤️ "There is nothing more important than the homeland." "We Mexicans, I say, have at least four loves." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Morelia, Michoacán She closed her report in Morelia, the land of José María Morelos, listing them: love for the family, love for one's neighbor, love for nature, which comes from the Indigenous peoples' love for Mother Earth, and love for the homeland. "And here in Michoacán, the homeland is loved."

🇲🇽📚 "Young people have nothing to do near a criminal group." "Why do we build schools? Because young people have to be in school. Why do we give scholarships? So that young people are in school… They have to be embraced by the government and their families, in school." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Morelia, Michoacán Every student in Michoacán now has a scholarship from primary school to university: 256,373 primary schoolchildren received the supplies and uniforms grant, 189,417 secondary students the Rita Cetina scholarship, 128,204 high-school students the Benito Juárez scholarship, and university students the Gertrudis Bocanegra scholarship, named after a Michoacán independence heroine.
banner: "YOUNG PEOPLE HAVE TO BE IN SCHOOL"

text: 🇲🇽🛣️ Plan Michoacán: more than 50 billion pesos for the state. "In total, 1,682,500 michoacanos and michoacanas receive a well-being program. It is an investment of 37,376 million pesos delivered directly." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Morelia, Michoacán Launched about a year ago, Plan Michoacán includes the finished Pátzcuaro–Uruapan highway modernization, upgrades to the Zitácuaro–Maravatío, Uruapan–Nueva Italia and Nueva Italia–Lázaro Cárdenas highways, the new Uruapan–Zamora highway, 54 hand-built rural roads, the recovery of Lake Pátzcuaro with three treatment plants, 88 water and drainage works, 19 new high schools, three Rosario Castellanos university campuses and 705 free doctor's offices.
